title: Grand Hotel
statementMd:
![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c9dce73d6b070949aa44ac38c46d54b32960d02e.png)The Grand Hotel, from commons.wikimedia.org, showing (nearly full) Nordic unity.

Four-Dimensional Grid World needs a new hotel to accommodate the next tourist season. Your task is to design the floor plan of this hotel. The hotel is to be built in a four-dimensional grid of $400 \times 400 \times 400 \times 400$ cells.

- A cell is a quadruple $(x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4)$ of integers, each between $0$ and $399$ inclusive.
- The distance between two cells $(x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4)$ and $(y_1, y_2, y_3, y_4)$ is $\sum_{i=1}^{4} |x_i - y_i|$ (sometimes called the Manhattan or $L_1$ distance).
- Two cells are adjacent if the distance between them is $1$.
- A set $H$ of cells is a hotel if the graph with vertex set $H$ and an edge between every pair of adjacent cells in $H$ is a tree. The rooms of the hotel are the leaves of this tree, that is, the cells of $H$ that are adjacent to exactly one other cell of $H$.

You are given a set $R$ of at least two cells, any two of which are at distance at least $15$. Construct a hotel with at most $10^6$ cells whose rooms are exactly the cells in $R$.

## Input

The input consists of:

- One line with an integer $n$ ($2 \leq n \leq 100$), the number of rooms.
- $n$ lines, each with four integers $x_1$, $x_2$, $x_3$, $x_4$ ($0 \leq x_i \leq 399$), the coordinates of a room.

Any two rooms are at distance at least $15$.

## Output

Output an integer $k$ ($1 \leq k \leq 10^6$), the number of cells of the hotel, followed by $k$ lines, each with four integers $x_1$, $x_2$, $x_3$, $x_4$ ($0 \leq x_i \leq 399$), the coordinates of a cell of the hotel. The cells must be distinct.

It can be shown that a solution always exists. If there are multiple valid solutions, you may output any one of them.
